clue.text: An inch out perhaps, but maintaining contact

indicators.note: perhaps tells the solver these letters are only one possible arrangement, to be reordered

explanation.surface: A measurement slightly off, yet still touching something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging INCHOUT; 'An' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in touch is to keep up communication with someone, which is keeping contact.

clue.text: I'm old fashioned, there's no getting away from it

definitions.text: there's no getting away from it

parts.note: taken as the letters, apostrophe dropped
passé means out of date or old fashioned

explanation.surface: A self-confessed fogey resigned to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock or dead end is a situation with no exit.

clue.text: Rude tot has to be made to be taught

indicators.note: the letters have to be made into something new, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: A rude child must be brought into line by lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructed privately by a tutor, which is being taught.

clue.text: A league match

explanation.definitionFit: An alliance of groups is one sense; a marriage or joining together is the other.

clue.text: Restricted by petty rules, as some in the library

explanation.definitionFit: Narrow and set in old ways is the first sense; volumes bound in leather are the second.

clue.text: Mention how to rear children

explanation.definitionFit: To raise a subject is to mention it, and to raise children is to rear them; the phrasal verb covers both.

clue.text: Freely born with vote in New York borough

indicators.note: freely means without fixed order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an X is the mark made on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: Born free and enfranchised in a New York district.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five boroughs of New York City, an example of such a borough.

clue.text: Peevishness "i shall moderate

parts.note: I shall contracts to I'll
to temper something is to moderate it

explanation.surface: Someone promising to calm their irritability.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpiness or crossness is a bad mood, which is peevishness.

clue.text: Given protection, being cautious

explanation.definitionFit: Watched over by a sentry is one sense; wary and reserved in speech is the other.

clue.text: Put on an act in front of nurse

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before or in front of
to nurse someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A performer acting the part before a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign or make believe is to act a part.

clue.text: Window panes need to be placed and fastened

parts.note: placed means put
fastened means tied

explanation.surface: Glazing instructions: the panes must be positioned and secured.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass in a window frame is sealed in with a soft cement, which is how panes are held fast.

clue.text: Not required for work, a number retire with consent

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the short form for number is read backwards

parts.note: No. is the usual abbreviation for number
leave means permission or consent

explanation.surface: Someone off duty steps back with permission from the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on authorised absence from duty is not needed at work for that period.

clue.text: Its owner can't be said to have a weak chest!

definitions.text: Its owner can't be said to have a weak chest!

parts.words: Its owner can't be said to have a weak chest!
parts.note: a weak chest sounds medical, but the chest is a box for valuables built to be secure

explanation.surface: A joke about someone whose lungs are notably healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe or reinforced container for valuables is a sturdy chest, the opposite of a feeble one.

clue.text: In short, Edward is opposed to the current trend, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for a contrary swirl of water is spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: an eddy is a swirl of water running against the main current

explanation.surface: A man named Edward who goes against fashion, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar shortened form of the name Edward, as in a pet name.

clue.text: Bear has no right to invest

indicators.note: has no means a letter is taken away from the word for bear

parts.note: to bear something is to endure it

explanation.surface: A bear with no rights trying to put money into shares.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone with a quality is to endow or furnish them with it, an old literary sense.

clue.text: Wrong, or sure one is wrong

indicators.note: is wrong says these letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insisting they are certain that a thing is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken or incorrect, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Given a free passage?

parts.note: a free passage suggests a free trip, but here it means a way that nothing blocks

explanation.surface: Someone handed a complimentary voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with nothing obstructing it moves on unhindered, its way clear.

clue.text: Idle ideas turned out to be made perfect

indicators.note: turned out means the letters are turned about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Lazy notions turned out to be flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown as better than in reality, so presented as flawless.

clue.text: Bird which is not all crest

parts.note: not all of something is only part of it
a crest is the top of a hill, a ridge

explanation.surface: A bird whose head plumage is incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump game bird shot in season, an example of a bird.

clue.text: A roof may be tarred

explanation.definitionFit: A sloping roof has a slant; coated with black resin is the other sense.

clue.text: Rum soul, perhaps, the brother of Remus

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An odd character who might be the twin of Rome's co-founder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman legend the twins founded Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the founder of Rome was suckled by a wolf with his twin.

clue.text: Goes on the roller-coaster, perhaps

parts.note: taking a turn on a fairground attraction, the roller-coaster being one example among many

explanation.surface: A fairground visitor taking a trip on the big dipper.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a turn on a fairground attraction is what a visitor does there, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Area inside American bases

parts.note: American bases sounds military, but these are the four bases of a baseball field

explanation.surface: A zone within US military bases.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the infield square marked by the bases is called by the name of a gemstone shape.

clue.text: Kind of labour we get fed up about

indicators.note: about means the word for fed up goes around we

parts.note: sated means full, fed up

explanation.surface: We get fed up with a certain type of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweated labour is work done for very low pay in poor conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploited work in poor conditions for low wages is a type of labour.

clue.text: Athenian method of working in metal

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for method goes inside the metal

parts.note: tin is a metal
MO stands for modus operandi, a method of working

explanation.surface: A Greek craftsman's technique for working with metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is the title figure of Shakespeare's play, a citizen of that Greek city.

clue.text: Grow crops-pretty vital, perhaps, inside

indicators.note: inside means the rearranged letters go into the word for pretty

parts.note: pretty means cute

indicators.note: perhaps tells the solver the letters of vital are to be reordered

explanation.surface: Farming crops is pretty vital work, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns VITAL into LTIVA, and 'inside' puts it inside CUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To till land and raise plants on it is to farm, which means growing crops.

clue.text: Calls for views to be expressed

indicators.note: expressed means spoken, so the word for views is said out loud

parts.note: sights are views

explanation.surface: Demands for opinions to be voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone to appear in court, as a legal sense of summon.

clue.text: Drive for mile trip round pithead

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the letter from the pit
trip suggests stumbling, so the letters are tripped into a new order

parts.note: the head of pit is its first letter P

explanation.surface: A drive for a mile's journey around a mine entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' turns MILE into IMEL, and 'round' puts it around P.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge or force forward is to propel, which is to drive.

clue.text: Offer, or wait for a better offer

explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to extend it, and to resist settling until terms improve is the second sense.

clue.text: Drink alcohol as a prop

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is a fortified wine, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone leaning on a drink to keep themselves upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something that holds a thing up, a brace or stay.

clue.text: Stops in crooked side streets

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: STS is the abbreviation for streets

explanation.surface: Someone halts in winding back alleys.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease or leave off doing something is to halt, the verb's meaning.

clue.text: A number baffled and deceived

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
to elude someone is to baffle or escape their understanding

explanation.surface: Several people were confused and misled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be misled into believing something false is to be fooled.
